physical power or mental resilience

a large number or amount of something

the act of determining the total number of something; the resulting total

A group of related things that belong together or are used together.

a quantity of something.
the act of evaluating two or more things to note similarities and differences.
the mathematical process of splitting a number into equal parts.

The mathematical operation of combining equal groups to find a total, represented by multiplying numbers or quantities.
A number written with a point, such as 0.5 or 2.75.
An unlimited extent, amount, or number; something without an end or limit.
An unbounded mathematical quantity or concept, represented by the symbol ∞, that is greater than every finite quantity in a relevant context.
The mathematical operation of taking one number or quantity away from another.
The product of all positive integers from 1 up to a given positive integer; written as n!.
An extremely small quantity or amount; especially a quantity approaching zero in mathematics.
The number of elements in a set, whether finite or infinite.
A scalar associated with a linear transformation or square matrix such that there is a nonzero vector that the transformation maps to the scalar multiple of itself.

A measure of how two variables change together: a positive value indicates that they tend to increase or decrease together, while a negative value indicates that one tends to increase as the other decreases.
A discrete, indivisible amount of a physical quantity, especially energy, as described by quantum theory.
A numerical measure of the size or strength of a quantity, especially in mathematics or physics.
The speed of an object in a specified direction.
A value obtained by measuring something, usually expressed with a number and a unit.
The rate at which a particular word, sound, letter, or other item occurs in a body of text or data.
The number of times a particular value or range of values occurs in a statistical dataset.
The ratio of useful output to total input in a process, machine, or system, often expressed as a percentage.
The proportion of a population that has a particular disease, condition, or characteristic at a given time or during a specified period.
An interval between two musical notes in which the higher note has twice the frequency of the lower note; specifically, a span of eight diatonic notes.
The proportion of light or other radiation reflected by a surface, especially a planet, moon, or other astronomical body, expressed as a value from zero to one or as a percentage.
A number or amount greater than that of any other option, but not necessarily more than half of the total; the largest share.
The amount of money repaid for an expense or payment.
The amount by which one quantity is greater or less than another; the result of subtracting one number from another.
The complete amount or number resulting from adding or combining parts.
A number calculated by adding a set of numbers and dividing the total by how many numbers there are; the arithmetic mean.
A typical amount, level, standard, or value calculated from or representing a group.
More than half of a total number or amount; the greater part.
The number of votes or members by which one side exceeds the other in a decision or election.
The amount of a specified substance contained in something.
The measurement of how tall someone or something is, especially from bottom to top.
The size, area, length, or range of something.
The amount of a substance that fills a cup.
A number or set of numbers representing points gained in a game, test, or competition.
The desire or need for a product or service among consumers, often considered in relation to its availability or price.
In chess, a tempo is the time or move advantage a player gains or loses, often by making a move that forces the opponent to respond.
In chess, the time control is the amount of time each player is allowed for a game or for a specified number of moves.
In tennis, love is a score of zero points in a game.
In baseball, the count is the number of balls and strikes recorded against a batter during an at-bat.
A statistic in baseball that measures how often a batter gets a hit, calculated by dividing hits by official at-bats.
In cricket, a run is one point scored when the batters complete a run between the wickets or score in another permitted way.
In golf, the standard number of strokes an expert golfer is expected to take to complete a hole or course.
In golf, a numerical measure of a player's ability used to adjust scores so players of different skill levels can compete fairly.
In go, a number of points added to White’s score to compensate for Black’s first-move advantage.
In boxing, the weight class for fighters above the sport’s heavyweight limit in lower divisions; its minimum weight limit is 200 pounds in professional boxing.
A boxing weight class for fighters whose weight falls within the division’s prescribed limits.
A boxing weight class for fighters whose weight is above the lightweight limit and no more than 147 pounds (66.7 kilograms) in professional boxing.
A boxing weight class for fighters who weigh no more than the featherweight limit, below the lightweight class.
A boxing weight class for fighters weighing up to 118 pounds (53.5 kilograms) in professional boxing.
A boxing weight division for fighters weighing no more than 112 pounds (about 50.8 kilograms).
A boxing weight division for fighters who weigh no more than 135 pounds (61.2 kilograms) in professional boxing.
The rate at which a cyclist turns the pedals, usually measured in revolutions per minute.
A rank or grade above the beginner levels in martial arts or go, typically awarded to advanced practitioners.
In backgammon, a pip is one point of distance that a checker moves when traveling between board points.
A student rank below dan in a martial art or wrestling ranking system.
A judgment or calculation of the approximate size, amount, value, or cost of something.
The money a movie, play, or other entertainment production earns from ticket sales.
A constant is a value that does not change within a particular mathematical or scientific context.
A literacy rate is the proportion of people in a population who can read and write.
A position in a number that determines the value of the digit occupying it.
A part or share of something larger, especially an amount allocated to someone or something.
A value representing zero or the absence of data, especially in computing or mathematics.
An order of magnitude is a scale of size expressed as a power of ten, or more generally a degree of size used to compare quantities.
A specified size or extent of an object, especially one used when making, fitting, or describing it.
A vector quantity describing the straight-line change from an object's starting position to its ending position, including direction.
The rate or regularity with which something happens or is repeated over a period of time.
An informal, emphatic large amount of something.
A reduction in spending or in the amount spent, or the amount thereby saved.
A system of weights and measures based on British units such as the inch, foot, pound, and gallon.
Market penetration is the extent to which a product, service, or idea has been adopted or reached within a market or population.
The area of a floor or building, expressed in square feet.
The highest or most intense point of a period, activity, or condition.
The distance of a point above a reference level, especially above the ground or sea.
The high-end is the uppermost or most expensive part of a market, product range, or category.
An atom is an extremely small amount or a minute unit of something, especially in figurative use.
The amount of a substance present in a given amount of a mixture or solution.
An amount of money equal to five cents in U.S. or Canadian currency.
The amount of light that reaches photographic film or a camera sensor when an image is captured, affecting how light or dark the image appears.
The total amount of something made or grown, especially goods, crops, or a natural resource, during a particular period.

concept_label: neighborhood (approximate amount; in the neighborhood of)
concept_definition: A range or approximate amount close to a stated number or value.

disambiguation.en: approximate amount; in the neighborhood of

concept_definition: A very small amount of something, especially when used with a modifier such as 'not an ounce' or 'every ounce'.
A very small amount of money; a trivial sum.
The amount of rain that falls in a particular place during a particular period, usually measured in millimeters or inches.
A number or percentage showing how many people watch or listen to a particular television or radio program, or the program's audience share.
A sloping position or angle; the degree to which something is tilted from horizontal or vertical.
The likelihood or probability that something will happen, often expressed as a ratio or as the chance of winning against a particular stake.
An amount that is greater than what is needed, used, or expected; an excess.
The permitted amount of variation from a specified measurement, limit, or standard.
The highest or most successful point in a process, career, or development; the peak.
The total mass of living organisms in a given area, habitat, or population, usually measured at a particular time.
The number or proportion of deaths in a population during a specified period, often from a particular cause.
The number of people present at an event or place.
The distance from one side of something to the other; how wide it is.
The extent, range, or variety of something, especially knowledge, experience, or activity.
An amount that can be held in one hand, especially a small quantity of something.
An amount by which one thing exceeds or falls short of another; a difference or gap.
A reserve or extra amount that provides room for error, variation, or unexpected events.
The distance from one end or side of something to the other; its width or extent.
The greatest possible amount, degree, or extent; the highest limit.
A shortage or amount by which something is less than what is needed, expected, or required.
A shortfall in points or goals that a competitor or team must overcome to catch up or win.
A small amount or degree of something.
An extremely large number or great variety of people or things.
A tiny amount of something; a trace or bit.
The maximum amount that something can contain, hold, or accommodate.
The greatest amount that a person, organization, or system can produce, process, or handle.
The distance from the top or surface of something to its bottom or deepest point.
The extent or degree of something, especially how far it reaches, develops, or affects people.
The distance below the surface of water, or a region far below that surface.
The greatest possible degree or extent; the limit of something.
The greatest amount, number, or degree that is possible, allowed, or attained.
The amount of something produced, especially by a person, machine, organization, or industry.
One part in every hundred; used to express a rate, proportion, or share per hundred, often with a number.
The likelihood or chance that a particular event or outcome will happen, often expressed as a number between 0 and 1 or as a percentage.
A comparative relationship between the size, amount, or degree of two or more things.
A part or share of a whole, considered in relation to the whole or to other parts.
An amount or number of something, especially when it can be measured or counted.
A considerable amount or number of something; a large quantity.
The total amount or totality of something, especially when considered as the result of several parts or factors.
A quantity or factor that can take different values or be changed, especially in mathematics, science, or an experiment.
The amount or value of something, especially when measured in money or in a quantity that will last for a stated period.
A change in a quantity, especially the difference between its final and initial values; commonly represented by the Greek letter Δ.
The angular distance of a place east or west of the prime meridian, measured in degrees.
The amount or concentration of dissolved salts in water or another substance.
The maximum extent or magnitude of a varying quantity, especially the maximum displacement of a wave or oscillation from its equilibrium position.
A measure of how much an investment or portfolio tends to move in relation to the overall market.
The distribution of a population, objects, or values across a range or area; the extent to which they are spread out rather than clustered.
A thermodynamic quantity that measures how energy in a system is dispersed or unavailable for doing work; in an isolated system, it does not decrease over time.
A standard or measure used to assess or judge something.
The thickness, diameter, or other measurable size of a material or object, often specified by a standard.
The degree of steepness of a slope or road, often expressed as a ratio or percentage.
The amount of water vapor present in the air.
A value, amount, or description that is close to the exact one but not exact.
The distance around a closed curved shape, especially a circle; the length of its boundary.
In statistics, the amount by which a value differs from a reference value, such as the mean.
A difference between two things, especially a difference in amount, rate, or degree.
A calculated or approximate figure for a quantity, cost, time, or other measurable amount.
A standard of measurement or a quantity used to assess or compare something, especially performance or progress.
A numerical or measurable factor that defines or helps determine the characteristics, behavior, or limits of a system, process, or situation.
The distance from a central point to the outer boundary of a circular or approximately circular area; the area reached from a particular center.
A large amount of something, especially when the amount is not stated precisely; often used in the phrase “a bunch of.”
A total amount or score calculated by combining several amounts or scores.
The rate or frequency at which something happens, especially the occurrence of a disease or other event within a population over a given period.
The amount of food, drink, or another substance taken into the body during a given period.
The chance or probability that something will happen or be true.
The distance or amount by which something is displaced from a reference point or position.
A position in an ordered list that shows how good, important, or successful someone or something is compared with others.
The measurement or regulation of how long something takes, or of the intervals and sequence of events, especially in a process or performance.
The extent or amount of something included, dealt with, or protected; the range or scope of coverage.
A small or limited part or amount of something; a tiny portion.
The large size, mass, or volume of something, especially when considered as a whole.
A limit or maximum amount placed on something.
The amount of a substance or quantity contained in a given space or area; especially, mass per unit volume.
An amount that is greater than what is usual, needed, or allowed; a surplus.
A very small amount or distance; a tiny degree or margin.
The smallest amount, number, or degree that is possible, allowed, or required.
The highest point, level, or value reached by something, especially during a period or process.
A large or more-than-sufficient amount or number of something.
A proportional relationship between the number of people or things in two groups, especially the number of one group for each member of another.
The number or amount of goods or services sold, especially during a particular period.
The extent or range of what something includes, covers, or can affect.
A very slow rate of movement or progress.
A person's or animal's height, especially when standing upright.
A very large quantity or amount of something; more than enough.
The number of copies of a newspaper, magazine, or other publication that are distributed or sold over a given period.
A numerical measure or indicator that represents the relative level, change, or condition of something, often calculated from a group of data.
The smaller part of a whole, or a number or proportion that is less than half of a group.
A proportion or rate expressed as a number of parts per hundred, often followed by the symbol %.
The distance between the two opposite surfaces of something; how thick it is.
The measurement of how wide something is, especially the distance from one side to the other; breadth.
